newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UN's Annan "hopeful" can avoid Kinshasa bloodshed.
newsitem.headline: UN's Annan "hopeful" can avoid Kinshasa bloodshed.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Saturday he was "hopeful" that negotiators could avert a bloody conflict in Kinshasa and arrange a peaceful transition to democratic elections in Zaire.

Speaking at a news conference in Moscow, he said: "We have not given up hope of getting the parties to accept some sort of a transitional arrangement and therefore avoid bloody conflict in the capital city...I'm quite hopeful that we will be able to avoid bloodshed in Kinshasa."

Annan said he also hoped mediators, who include United Nations special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun and senior South African officials, could convince rebel leader Laurent Kabila to form a broad-based coalition government before elections were held.
Kabila said on Saturday he was taking over as head of state with the agreement of generals in Kinshasa and he expected the capital to be in his hands in hours.
President Mobutu Sese Seko stepped aside and left Kinshasa on Friday after more than 30 years in power.
